SE.headline: Yellow Wind in the alpine region Parts of the northern Lapland mountains
SE.description:
Windy with very strong westerly winds on the bare mountains and also occasional heavy rainfall.; What happens?: Friday evening increasing westerly wind which on the bare mountains can become very strong, 18-24 m/s. The wind culminates on Saturday with locally up to storm 25 m/s. Precipitation is also expected at times, both as rain and sleet.; What should I think about?: Do not hike in mountainous areas if you are inexperienced.
It can be difficult to move and set up or anchor tents.
In connection with drifting snow, it can be difficult to orientate due to reduced visibility.

GB.headline: Areas of fog developing this evening and overnight, dense in places: UPDATED
GB.description:
Information on update: Parts of East Anglia removed from warning, which has also been extended a little further west and northwest to account for latest observations and data. Clearing skies over southeast England this evening and overnight, which has already led to the development of mist and some patchy fog, is likely to allow increasingly widespread and in places dense fog to form. Visibility will fall below 100m in some places. The fog will gradually lift and clear to mist and haze during Saturday morning, persisting longest where visibilities are poorest early on.

For further details see
areas: East Midlands | East of England | London & South East England | West Midlands

GB.headline: Fog, dense in places, may lead to some travel disruption on Saturday night and Sunday morning
GB.description:
Patchy, dense fog is expected to develop during Saturday night with the visibility falling to less than 50 metres in places. Fog is expected to become increasingly widespread within this area during the second half of the night before only slowly clearing during Sunday morning; slowest across parts of the West Country and central southern England.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings
areas: East Midlands | London & South East England | South West England | West Midlands
